findings.item: Scope: which redeployed services run migrations at boot
findings.detail: Of the services being rebuilt, four apply migrations when they start: session-core (sqlx, `_sqlx_migrations` table), capability-core (psql loop with no ledger), org-core (`schema_migrations`) and audit-core (`schema_migrations`, from an embedded list). model-gateway, execution-core and inference-core embed no migrator: a grep for `sqlx::migrate!` outside session-core found nothing. The org-core call is at cmd/server/main.go:71, not cmd/main.go. Every diff entry for the four migration dirs is 'A' (added). No existing migration file was changed, so already-applied files keep their checksums in git. The working-tree line-ending caveat for session-core is a separate finding below.
findings.evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/main.rs:74 -> store.rs:84-89; capability-core/docker-entrypoint.sh:9-15; apps/Control Plane/org-core/cmd/server/main.go:71 -> internal/database/migrate.go:26-72; apps/Control Plane/audit-core/cmd/server/main.go:54 -> internal/store/migrate.go:45-56,67-115; `git diff --name-status <rev> HEAD` shows only A entries

findings.item: session-core: list of new migrations (4bf17b08..HEAD)
findings.detail: Eleven new forward files: 0049, 0050, 0051, 0052, 0055, 0056, 0057, 0058, 0064, 0067 and 0068, plus matching revert/*.down.sql. sqlx skips the revert/ subdirectory. The running image already had 0054_run_questions, so 0049-0052 are numbered below a version that is already applied. sqlx 0.8.6 (Cargo.lock:4131-4132) applies unapplied versions in order and does not refuse out-of-order ones. I am fairly but not fully sure of that from memory of sqlx's Migrator::run, so check after boot that rows 49-52 exist.

findings.item: session-core 0049_thread_activity_cursor
findings.detail: What it does: adds threads.last_activity_at (NOT NULL DEFAULT now()), backfills it from each thread's newest message for every thread, and builds a keyset index. Idempotent: yes (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, a repeatable UPDATE, CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS). Can it fail on existing data: no. The NOT NULL has a default, pinned_at exists (0021:11) and there are no triggers on threads. It is a full-table UPDATE plus a non-concurrent index build on threads, so it locks threads briefly. Rollback: the old image keeps working, since inserts get the default. However, the old code never advances last_activity_at, so threads written during a rollback window sort stale once HEAD is back, and nothing re-backfills them.
findings.evidence: session-core/migrations/0049_thread_activity_cursor.sql:12-22

findings.item: session-core 0050_thread_autonomy_grant
findings.detail: What it does: adds five nullable grant columns on threads and a CHECK, granted_rung IN (read_only, workspace_write, danger_full_access), added NOT VALID and then validated. Idempotent: yes (DO block guard). Can it fail on existing data: no, every existing value is NULL. Rollback: the old code ignores the columns. HEAD checks once at boot whether the columns exist (grpc.rs:503), so after a manual revert session-core must be restarted.
findings.evidence: 0050_thread_autonomy_grant.sql:32-55; src/grpc.rs:503

findings.item: session-core 0051_user_memory_state
findings.detail: What it does: adds user_memory_controls.memory_state (default 'on') with a validated CHECK, two nullable columns, and a new content-free table memory_control_events. Idempotent: yes. Can it fail on existing data: no, existing rows take 'on'. Rollback: harmless. The old code never writes the new table, but it also never erases it.
findings.evidence: 0051_user_memory_state.sql:25-61

findings.item: session-core 0052_message_client_id
findings.detail: What it does: adds a nullable messages.client_message_id, a regex CHECK (NOT VALID, then VALIDATE) and a partial unique index on (thread_id, client_message_id) WHERE NOT NULL. Idempotent: yes. Can it fail on existing data: no. Every existing row is NULL, so the unique index has no entries, but VALIDATE still scans messages. Rollback: harmless.
findings.evidence: 0052_message_client_id.sql:25-46

findings.item: session-core 0055_message_search_index (no-transaction)
findings.detail: What it does: runs CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS for a GIN full-text index on messages (user and assistant rows). The file is marked `-- no-transaction` and holds a single statement, so the simple-protocol execution is not wrapped in an implicit transaction. Idempotent: only in name. If the build fails part way, an INVALID index is left behind. sqlx writes its ledger row only after the SQL succeeds, so the next boot re-runs the file, IF NOT EXISTS skips the invalid index, and the migration is recorded as successful with an unusable index. The file itself warns about this. Can it fail or hang: CONCURRENTLY waits for every older open transaction in the session_core database. Seven services share that database (orchestrator-core, execution-core, letta-bridge and others), so one idle-in-transaction connection can stall session-core's boot indefinitely. The sqlx advisory lock is held meanwhile, so a second session-core replica would also wait. Rollback: harmless to the old code.
findings.evidence: 0055_message_search_index.sql:1,12-19; deploy/docker-compose.yml:812,1295,1545,1623,1901,1944,2085 (all DATABASE_URL .../session_core)

findings.item: session-core 0058_agent_skills_proposals: rolling session-core back breaks skill upserts
findings.detail: What it does: adds review_state (default 'accepted') with a validated CHECK and three defaulted columns. It creates the unique index agent_skills_scope_owner_name_uq on (org_id, scope, owner_user_id, name), then DROPS agent_skills_org_name_uq. Idempotent: yes. Can it fail on existing data: no. The old unique (org_id, name) from 0004:205-206 implies the new key, and the new index is a plain build, not CONCURRENTLY. Rollback: BREAKS. The old session-core UpsertSkill uses `ON CONFLICT (org_id, name)` (old grpc.rs:5603). With the index gone, Postgres rejects it with 'no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification'. The migration's own contract line says to roll back only together with revert/0058. Old capability-core is not affected: its skill INSERT has no ON CONFLICT (old registry_apis.go:215).
findings.evidence: 0058_agent_skills_proposals.sql:19,23-52; git show 4bf17b08:.../session-core/src/grpc.rs:5598-5603

findings.item: session-core 0064_skill_revisions: a trigger on a table two services write
findings.detail: What it does: creates the skill_revisions table, two plpgsql functions, and an AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE trigger on agent_skills. Every write from session-core or capability-core then logs a revision that includes a snapshot of the skill content. Idempotent: yes (CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER needs PG14+, and gen_random_uuid needs PG13+; Model Plane postgres is 16.14, deploy/docker-compose.yml:31,154). Can it fail on existing data: no backfill, so no. The trigger never raises: an unattributed writer is logged as 'unattributed'. Rollback: the old images can still write. But the old session-core org erasure runs `DELETE FROM agent_skills WHERE org_id` (old gdpr.rs:390) and never deletes skill_revisions. The trigger turns each deleted skill into a 'deleted' revision that holds the skill text, so content survives an org erasure. HEAD deletes skill_revisions after agent_skills (gdpr.rs:396,405). That is a GDPR/ZDR regression if session-core is rolled back without revert/0064.
findings.evidence: 0064_skill_revisions.sql:32-52,100-181; src/gdpr.rs:396,405; git grep 4bf17b08 gdpr.rs:390 (no skill_revisions)

findings.item: session-core 0067_thread_memory_mode and 0068_thread_memory_resumed_at
findings.detail: What they do: 0067 adds threads.memory_mode (default 'inherit') with a validated CHECK. 0068 adds a nullable memory_resumed_at. Idempotent: yes. Can they fail on existing data: no. Rollback: harmless to old writes, but the old code ignores a per-thread 'off'.
findings.evidence: 0067_thread_memory_mode.sql:19-35; 0068_thread_memory_resumed_at.sql:16

findings.item: session-core: the old image cannot boot over the new schema
findings.detail: The 4bf17b08 binary calls `sqlx::migrate!("./migrations").run(pool)` in strict mode. It has no SESSION_CORE_MIGRATION_IGNORE_MISSING switch; that switch exists only in the HEAD binary. Once versions 49-68 are applied, the old image fails at boot with VersionMissing(49) before serving anything. Rolling back therefore means: apply revert/0068..0049 in reverse order, delete those rows from _sqlx_migrations, then start the old image. Setting the env var does nothing for the old binary.
findings.evidence: git show 4bf17b08:.../session-core/src/store.rs:33-34; HEAD store.rs:10-15,54-75

findings.item: session-core: checksum mismatch from CRLF working-tree files (uncertain)
findings.detail: The session-core Dockerfile copies the working tree (`COPY rust/ rust/`), and sqlx checksums the bytes of each embedded file. In this worktree, files 0001-0034 are CRLF on disk but LF in git (`git ls-files --eol`: i/lf w/crlf, 34 files), even though .gitattributes:37 says `*.sql text eol=lf`. Their mtimes are 2026-09-06, so if the running 4bf17b08 image was built from this worktree, it embedded the same CRLF bytes and the checksums match. If the live database was migrated by an image built from an LF checkout (the main checkout, a fresh clone or CI), the HEAD image built here fails with VersionMismatch on the first CRLF file. I cannot tell which from the repo alone. Compare checksums before deploying.
findings.evidence: session-core/Dockerfile:20,33; .gitattributes:37; git ls-files --eol output (34 w/crlf: 0001..0034)

findings.item: Shared database session_core: session-core and capability-core
findings.detail: Yes, both point at session_core (deploy/docker-compose.yml:812 for session-core and :1623 for capability-core), along with orchestrator-core, execution-core, browser-broker, letta-bridge and cost-core. Their migration tables cannot collide. session-core uses sqlx's `_sqlx_migrations`, and capability-core keeps no ledger at all: it re-runs every *.up.sql with psql at each boot (docker-entrypoint.sh:9-15). No other Model Plane Go service references _sqlx_migrations or schema_migrations. No table name created by capability-core, orchestrator-core, cost-core, browser-broker or letta-bridge migrations matches a session-core table (comm over the CREATE TABLE names). They do touch each other's data, though. capability-core reads and writes session-core's agent_skills, and HEAD capability-core needs session-core 0058 columns (registry_apis.go:251,339,385,478,483). capability-core depends_on lists only temporal, nats and postgres (deploy/docker-compose.yml ~1600-1607). If capability-core HEAD starts before session-core HEAD has migrated, its skill endpoints fail with 'column review_state does not exist' until it does.
findings.evidence: deploy/docker-compose.yml:812,1623; capability-core/docker-entrypoint.sh:9-15; capability-core/internal/api/registry_apis.go:124,251,483

findings.item: capability-core: list of new migrations (4bf17b08..HEAD) and how they run
findings.detail: New files: 0017_tool_policies, 0020_result_query_capability, 0021_skill_bundles, 0022_agent_action_admissions, 0023_org_agent_policy, 0024_provider_read_tool and 0025_tool_policies_allow_needs_digest; there are no 0018 or 0019. The runner re-applies all 25 files, old and new, on every boot. It uses psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 with no single-transaction flag, so a file without its own BEGIN commits statement by statement, and a failure exits 1 and puts the container in a crash loop. The old files 0001-0016 are unchanged and already run on every HEAD boot after the new ones, so an old image re-running 0001-0016 over the new schema is proven safe.
findings.evidence: capability-core/docker-entrypoint.sh:9-15; git diff --name-status 4bf17b08 HEAD -- .../capability-core/migrations

findings.item: capability-core 0017_tool_policies
findings.detail: What it does: creates tool_policies, a partial unique 'one active policy' index and a capability index, and adds capabilities.policy_relaxable as GENERATED ALWAYS AS (kind = 'mcp_tool') STORED. Idempotent: yes, and stated so in the file. Can it fail on existing data: no, the table is new and the generated column is computed. Adding a stored generated column rewrites the capabilities table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock once. Rollback: old code never touches tool_policies, and its capabilities INSERTs don't name the generated column, so nothing breaks.
findings.evidence: 0017_tool_policies.up.sql:35-65

Idempotent: yes. ON CONFLICT (id) / (org_id, capability_id, tool_name), and the tool row is re-asserted only WHERE source = 'seed'. Can they fail on existing data: the values satisfy the 0016 CHECKs (0016:49-54,81-90). The qualified_name unique index (0016:99-101) does not apply because qualified_name is NULL. findings.item: capability-core 0025_tool_policies_allow_needs_digest
findings.detail: What it does: inside its own BEGIN/COMMIT, it revokes every live 'allow' policy that has no digest (sets revoked_at and updated_at), then adds a validated CHECK, `decision <> 'allow' OR pinned_digest IS NOT NULL OR revoked_at IS NOT NULL`, guarded by a pg_constraint lookup. Idempotent: yes. Can it fail on existing data: no, because the UPDATE removes every row that would violate the CHECK before it is added. This is the one migration that changes existing rows, and the revocation is not undone by the down file (I did not read the down file). On the live database tool_policies does not exist yet unless an earlier proof run created it, so it most likely touches nothing. 0017 runs first in the same boot, so the `'tool_policies'::regclass` cast resolves. Rollback: the old image has no code for tool_policies, so nothing breaks.
findings.evidence: 0025_tool_policies_allow_needs_digest.up.sql:25-49

Can they fail on existing data: no, all tables are new, the FKs point at organizations(id), and the limit trigger is on a new empty table. findings.item: org-core 024_org_core_app_least_privilege
findings.detail: What it does: runs REVOKE ALL and then narrower GRANTs to org_core_app on the nine tables from 021-023, because 009's default privileges had silently given all four privileges. Idempotent: yes. Can it fail on existing data: no data is involved. It needs the role and tables, which 009 and 021-023 provide in the same boot. Runtime check of HEAD code against the narrowed grants: FOR UPDATE/SHARE (which needs UPDATE) is used only on tables that keep UPDATE. Those are org_browser_site_policy (browsersites/repository.go:368-370), org_model_policy_revisions (modelentitlement/repository.go:221) and siem_destinations (siem_destinations.go:615,680). The user_browser_site_prefs upsert keeps UPDATE. The outbox claim and mark statements (siem_destinations.go:800-884) run on r.pool, outside the WithOrgScope SET LOCAL ROLE (database.go:97-114), so they do not need UPDATE as org_core_app. I did not check every code path. A write I missed would fail at runtime with 'permission denied', not at migration time. Rollback: the old image does not use these tables, so it is harmless.
findings.evidence: 024_org_core_app_least_privilege.up.sql:15-60; internal/database/database.go:75,97-114

findings.item: audit-core 007_audit_chain: append-only trigger breaks old retention on rollback
findings.detail: What it does: adds five nullable chain columns to audit_events, a validated chain_mode CHECK, a partial unique index on (org_id, chain_seq), and the audit_chain_heads table. It also adds a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger, audit_events_guard, that RAISEs on any UPDATE or DELETE unless the transaction set audit.maintenance = 'on' or the update is the one-time chaining transition. Idempotent: yes (IF NOT EXISTS, DROP ... IF EXISTS, CREATE OR REPLACE), and it is ledgered. Can it fail on existing data: no, all new columns are NULL, so the CHECK and unique index pass. ALTER TABLE takes a short ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on audit_events. Rollback: BREAKS retention. The old Purge runs a plain `DELETE FROM audit_events WHERE ingested_at < ...` with no audit.maintenance. The trigger raises restrict_violation as soon as any row is past retention, and Purge returns before it purges usage_events, so usage retention stops too. The old runRetention only logs the error and keeps running. HEAD sets audit.maintenance before its deletes (store.go:290-303, attest.go:286-290). Inserts are unaffected: the old insert is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
findings.evidence: audit-core/internal/store/migrations/007_audit_chain.sql:14-83; git show 2f2c3e83:.../store/store.go:243-266; 2f2c3e83:.../cmd/server/main.go:157-165

Idempotent: yes (IF NOT EXISTS). Can they fail on existing data: no, they are additive and nothing on audit_events changes. Rollback: harmless.

steps: RISK-ORDERED LIST (highest first): (1) session-core rollback is blocked. The old image fails at boot with sqlx VersionMissing(49); even past that, 0058 breaks the old UpsertSkill ON CONFLICT (org_id, name), and 0064's trigger makes the old org erasure leave skill text in skill_revisions. Rolling back means applying revert/0068..0049 and deleting those _sqlx_migrations rows first. (2) session-core 0055 CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY can stall boot behind any open transaction in the shared session_core database; a failed build leaves an INVALID index that the next boot records as applied. (3) Possible sqlx checksum mismatch: session-core 0001-0034 are CRLF in this worktree, which matters only if the live database was migrated by an image built from an LF checkout. (4) audit-core 007 trigger: rolling audit-core back to 2f2c3e83 silently stops audit and usage retention. (5) Deploy order: capability-core HEAD needs session-core 0058, and compose does not order them. (6) capability-core 0025 revokes digest-less live allows; it changes data but most likely matches nothing live. (7) org-core 024 grant narrowing: a write path the narrowing missed would fail at runtime. (8) session-core 0049 full-table UPDATE of threads, and timestamps drift if rolled back. (9) All other new migrations are additive (none to very low risk).

PRE-DEPLOY, session_core (read-only): run `SELECT version, success, encode(checksum,'hex') FROM _sqlx_migrations ORDER BY version;`. Expect max version 54 (versions 1-48 and 54), all success = t, and no version outside the HEAD file set. Then compare each checksum with `sha384sum "apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/migrations/00NN_*.sql"` for the bytes in this worktree. A mismatch on 0001-0034 means the HEAD image built here will fail with VersionMismatch.

PRE-DEPLOY, session_core: run `SELECT pid, usename, application_name, state, now()-xact_start AS age FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE datname='session_core' AND xact_start IS NOT NULL ORDER BY xact_start;`. Clear any long or idle-in-transaction sessions before session-core runs 0055.
DEPLOY ORDER: start session-core first and wait for its 'migrations applied' log (store.rs:87), then capability-core. org-core and audit-core are independent of each other.

findings.item: Addition: audit-core 007_audit_chain installs an append-only guard trigger, and rolling back to the old image breaks its retention purge
findings.detail: What it does: adds five nullable chain columns to audit_events, a CHECK on chain_mode (validated, but every existing value is NULL), a partial unique index on (org_id, chain_seq) WHERE chain_seq IS NOT NULL (empty at first), the audit_chain_heads table, and the BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger audit_events_guard. The trigger raises restrict_violation unless the transaction set audit.maintenance=on, or the update only fills the chain columns from NULL. Idempotent: yes, but the runner is ledgered, so it runs once in one transaction. Can it fail on existing data: no. Rollback: BREAKS. The old 2f2c3e83 Purge runs a bare `DELETE FROM audit_events WHERE ingested_at < NOW() - N days` without setting audit.maintenance. Once any row is older than the retention window (default 365 days), the guard makes it fail, and because Purge returns early, the usage_events purge is skipped too. HEAD sets audit.maintenance and skips chained rows (store.go:290-307). The depth register accepted this as intended and says to roll audit-core as one image swap (D1-294). Old INSERTs (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) are not affected. Separately, D1-292 warns that a rolling deploy lets an old replica write an unchained row just before activation, which is then never chained, so stop the old container before the new one starts.

The sharp edge: an unrecognised MODEL_ENTITLEMENT_MODE value is treated as 'enforce' (compose default is off). With the URL or token missing in shadow or enforce mode, every answer becomes unavailable rather than failing boot. Boot is also less strict than before: a ZDR attestation outside its in-force window now logs an ERROR and disables ZDR for that surface instead of failing boot. Other new switches are optional: INFERENCE_ANTHROPIC_TIERED_SYSTEM, INFERENCE_OPENAI_PROMPT_CACHE_KEY, INFERENCE_CORE_EFFORT_BUDGET_CLAMP, INFERENCE_CORE_CODEX_WIDE_EFFORT, INFERENCE_VISION_MODEL_DENYLIST_EXTRA.

findings.item: (2) Transcript paging needs session-core, model-gateway and the BFF together
findings.detail: model-gateway HEAD sends ListConversation with limit and before_message_id. The running session-core (4bf17b08b) has no fields 6 and 7. As proto3 unknown fields they are ignored, so it answers the full transcript with has_more=false. The failure is silent rather than a refusal, and the paging proof would fail on the page count and the has_more assertions. All three parts arrived in one commit (5c81e7f52): session-core grpc.rs, model-gateway http_routes.rs, and the verevonv3 gateway's chat/history.rs and json_handlers.rs. The proof reads through the BFF route /api/v1/chat/threads/{id}/messages and seeds session-core's database directly. Reverse direction is safe: an old model-gateway against session-core HEAD sends limit=0, which is the unchanged unpaged read.

If the per-service compose `up` is used without --no-deps, compose may recreate dependencies whose config changed (I am not certain of compose's exact behaviour), but nothing here depends on browser-broker. findings.item: (4) Which services can stay on their running image for each proof
findings.detail: Transcript paging: rebuild session-core, model-gateway and the verevonv3 BFF gateway (it must include 5c81e7f52; I do not know its running revision). These can stay: inference-core, execution-core, capability-core, browser-broker, org-core, audit-core. org-core migration 024: rebuild org-core only. 024 is GRANT/REVOKE on tables created by 021-023, which the same boot applies. It needs the Control Plane env to carry AUDIT_ORG_CORE_SERVICE_TOKEN, BROWSER_BROKER_ORG_CORE_SERVICE_TOKEN and INFERENCE_ORG_CORE_SERVICE_TOKEN (minted by run-control-plane.sh), and the auth-core principal must hold org:retention:read:any. Nothing in the Model Plane needs to change. capability-core migration 0025: rebuild capability-core only to apply 0025 at boot. But run it after session-core HEAD (migrations 0056, 0058 and GetMemoryControls) and after auth-core's registry is refreshed, or its cron sweeper, skills API, memory proxy and minted session-core calls break at runtime. Because the paging proof deploys session-core HEAD, doing paging first satisfies the schema half. audit-core chain-on: rebuild audit-core only and set AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED=1 in its env_file. The keys are optional in development and required with ENVIRONMENT=production. It does not depend on org-core (only the separate audit-siem-exporter profile does). Can stay for all three proofs: inference-core, execution-core, browser-broker. execution-core lists session-core and inference-core under depends_on and capability-core lists orchestrator-core, so redeploy with --no-deps to avoid recreating them.

Without them, HEAD compose interpolation fails for every Control Plane command.

Rebuild and recreate org-core from HEAD with --no-deps (scripts/run-control-plane.sh). It applies 021-024 at boot. Its credential registry needs the auth-core principal to hold org:retention:read:any (compose line 543 already grants it). Then run the 024 proof.

Rebuild and recreate audit-core from HEAD with AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED=1 set in its env_file (./audit-core/.env). In production, also set AUDIT_CHAIN_KEY_ID and AUDIT_CHAIN_PRIVATE_KEY_BASE64. Run the chain-on proof. Do not recreate the old audit-core or org-core images from HEAD compose.

Before the session-core deploy, read SELECT version FROM _sqlx_migrations in the session_core database. Confirm it holds no version that HEAD lacks (gaps 0053, 0054, 0059-0063, 0065, 0066), or HEAD's strict migrator will refuse to boot. Note that the running session-core image cannot be rolled back to without revert/*.down.sql once HEAD migrates.

Rebuild model-gateway from HEAD, then the verevonv3 BFF gateway at 5c81e7f52 or later. Per the memory notes, use recreate-with-live-env.sh after a worktree build. Then run scripts/tests/transcript-paging-proof.sh.

If auth-core is rebuilt instead, org-core HEAD must already be up. Then rebuild capability-core from HEAD with --no-deps so it applies 0017 and 0020-0025, and run the 0025 proof.

Leave inference-core, execution-core and browser-broker on their running images. Avoid project-wide `docker compose up` or build-verevon-services.sh --from model, which would recreate browser-broker onto the session_core database and drop its live grants.

findings.item: Verified as stated: transcript paging coupling (session-core + model-gateway + BFF)
findings.detail: Confirmed. ListConversationRequest gains limit=6 and before_message_id=7, and the response gains has_more=2. 5c81e7f52 is not an ancestor of 4bf17b08b. model-gateway HEAD forwards limit and before. session-core HEAD refuses a foreign cursor with InvalidArgument, which model-gateway maps to 400. The BFF validates limit (1-200), refuses before without limit, and proxies the model-gateway JSON unchanged, so the proof can read has_more and message_id at the top level. Against the running session-core, the extra fields are ignored and the full transcript comes back: the page count, has_more and 400 assertions all fail. The proof's seed INSERT fits the HEAD schema: text ids, origin defaults to 'chat', and the space/audience CHECKs pass with NULLs.

findings.item: Correction: the session-core org policy poller is probably NOT dormant on this stack
findings.detail: The report treats the poller as dormant because SESSION_ORG_CORE_SERVICE_TOKEN defaults to empty in the Model Plane compose. But scripts/compose.sh adds 'Control Plane/.env.generated-secrets' as an --env-file before deploy/.env. run-control-plane.sh mints SESSION_ORG_CORE_SERVICE_TOKEN into that file, because the Control Plane compose requires it (:?). Unless deploy/.env sets it to empty explicitly (I did not read it), session-core HEAD starts polling GET {ORG_CORE_URL}/internal/orgs/{org}/agent-policy for every org in threads. The running org-core (2f2c3e83a) has no agent-policy route, and its registry gives session-core only org:read:any. A 404 reads as the permissive defaults; a 403 or a network error logs a WARN and the mirror ages. With ORG_POLICY_FAIL_CLOSED=false (the default), memory behaviour does not change. findings.item: Other variables the chain uses (names only), and which ones each feature needs
findings.detail: A plain chained insert needs no key at all. The keys are AUDIT_CHAIN_KEY_ID, AUDIT_CHAIN_PRIVATE_KEY_BASE64, AUDIT_CHAIN_PUBLIC_KEY_BASE64 and AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY_KEYS (retired keys as key_id:pub, comma-separated). They are only read when the chain or pruning is on. Signed head attestations need KEY_ID plus PRIVATE_KEY: the attestor only starts when the chain is on and the key ring can sign, and it runs every AUDIT_CHAIN_ATTEST_INTERVAL (default 60s, minimum 1s). Retention pruning of chained rows needs AUDIT_CHAIN_PRUNE_ENABLED=1 and a private key; AUDIT_CHAIN_PRUNE_DRYRUN=1 wins over it. The verifier is switched by AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY_ENABLED: empty means it follows the chain, "0" turns it off. AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY_INTERVAL defaults to 24h. ENVIRONMENT=production makes the signing key mandatory when the chain is on. Compose passes all of these from interpolation, and the runner mints the audit-chain Ed25519 pair into the secrets ledger if it is missing and never overwrites an existing value.

findings.item: How an org's chain is activated, and legacy rows
findings.detail: There is no explicit activation step. An org's chain starts at its first chained insert. lockChainHead runs INSERT INTO audit_chain_heads (org_id, head_seq 0, head_hash = genesis) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; activated_at then takes DEFAULT NOW(), which is the start time of that transaction. Each chained insert locks the head row FOR UPDATE, checks that the stored tip row still has head_hash (a mismatch sets state='broken' once and the row is still appended), inserts the row, and in the same transaction sets chain_seq = head+1, prev_hash = the head hash, row_hash, chain_version=1 and chain_mode='insert', then advances the head. Rows of the org with ingested_at before activated_at stay chain_seq NULL for good (legacy_unchained); there is no backfill. Rows that arrive unchained after activation, while the switch is off, are chained by the boot CatchUp with chain_mode='catchup', in ingested_at,id order, before the subscriber starts. CatchUp only visits orgs that already have a head. The genesis prev_hash of seq 1 is sha256('VAC1/genesis/' || org_id).

findings.item: Checking the hash independently: the in-process verifier and the audit-verify CLI
findings.detail: (1) psql can check sequence contiguity, prev_hash = previous row_hash, head = last row, and the genesis hash (Postgres 15 has a built-in sha256()). Recomputing row_hash in SQL is not practical: it is a uvarint length-prefixed binary encoding with canonical details JSON. (2) The verifier inside audit-core runs one pass at boot and then every AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY_INTERVAL, recomputing every row. It writes audit_chain_verifications. A restart therefore triggers a full check, and the mid-stream restart doubles as a verify step. (3) audit-verify is at /usr/local/bin/audit-verify in the audit-core image. Usage: audit-verify [-manifest FILE] [-key-id ID -public-key BASE64] [-verify-keys LIST] [-json] PAGE..., with flags before the files. Its input is compliance-API exports: a bare manifest object (the `data` of GET /api/v1/audit/compliance/manifest) and the unchanged envelope pages of GET /api/v1/audit/compliance/events?limit=1000. Exit codes: 0 verified or verified_with_legacy, 2 broken, 3 partial, key_unavailable or unreadable input, 1 usage. Getting those pages requires an owner or admin session through the gateway with the compliance scope, which is still open live-proof work (D1-388, D1-391), so treat audit-verify as optional for D1-297. Runbook §10 says no code checks the manifest signature; that looks stale, because audit-verify now does check it.

findings.item: Which events reach audit-core on the dev stack
findings.detail: The primary bus controlplane-nats uses durables audit-core-control-v3-audit and -usage on subject verevon.audit.v2.control.> in stream VEREVON_CONTROL_OBSERVABILITY. Two named extra buses do the same: model-nats (verevon.audit.v2.model.>, durable audit-core-model-v3-audit) and application-nats (verevon.audit.v2.application.>). Subjects have the form verevon.audit.v2.<plane>.<producer>.<event>, and a subject whose plane, producer or event does not match the payload is terminated and dead-lettered. Producers: auth-core (control: sign_in and others), user-core and org-core outboxes (control), session-core outbox (model: tool_action_reserved, tool_action, approval_decided), leads-core (application). There is also a direct HTTP POST /v1/audit, but only integration-corev2 holds a token for it (audit:write, plane ingestion), so there is no credential-free service call. Publishing by hand on NATS would also need a producer credential.

findings.item: Restart mid-stream: why there should be no gap
findings.detail: The row insert and its chain position are committed in one transaction under the head lock, and the unique (org_id, chain_seq) index backs that up. audit-core acks the JetStream message only after the database write, with AckWait 30s and MaxDeliver 5. A message in flight when the container is killed is redelivered and then either inserted, or counted as a duplicate if it had already committed. A redelivered duplicate shows up as audit_core_chain_appends_total{result="duplicate"}. Note that the histogram is in-process and resets on restart, so capture it before and after, or read it through Prometheus.
findings.evidence: internal/store/chain.go:186-234; migrations/007_audit_chain.sql:30-32; internal/subscriber/subscriber.go:90-116, :193-207

findings.item: Metric audit_core_chain_head_lock_wait_seconds, and where to read it
findings.detail: This is a histogram with buckets 0.001 to 10s and no org label. It is observed on every chained insert and every catch-up batch, and the timing covers both the head-create upsert and the SELECT ... FOR UPDATE. Related series: audit_core_chain_appends_total{result}, audit_core_chain_broken_total, audit_core_details_guard_total, audit_core_chain_last_verify_timestamp_seconds (only while the verifier runs). /metrics is on port 9091 (METRICS_PORT), which is not published to the host; compose publishes only 127.0.0.1:8187. Read it inside the container with busybox wget at http://127.0.0.1:9091/metrics, or through Prometheus, which scrapes audit-core-service:9091 and is reachable on the host at 127.0.0.1:19095 (CONTROL_PROMETHEUS_HOST_PORT).

findings.item: Switching the chain OFF after the proof
findings.detail: This is supported and is step 1 of runbook §7: set AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED to 0 and recreate the container. New rows are then unchained; existing chained rows, heads, attestations and checkpoints are kept; the attestor and the verifier stop (so the VerifyStale alert's series disappears). When the switch is turned on again, boot CatchUp chains every row written while it was off and after activated_at, with chain_mode='catchup'. The guard trigger stays installed whatever the switch says: migration 007 always runs. The current image's Purge sets audit.maintenance and skips chained rows, so it works with the switch off. Never run the revert SQL files: they drop the chain for good. D1-294 risk: an image built from branch `main` (pre-S2) runs against the migrated schema. Its inserts work, because the new columns are nullable. Its Purge, however, deletes without the maintenance setting, and the trigger refuses as soon as at least one row is older than the 365-day retention. On a young dev database that may never happen; that is uncertain. Its rows would also be unchained and later caught up. In practice: until model-plane merges, do not rebuild audit-core from the main checkout once 007 is applied.

findings.item: Image provenance for the evidence
findings.detail: The runner sets SOURCE_REVISION=local unless the variable is already set, so the image's org.opencontainers.image.revision label shows 'local'. Runbook §9 asks for the image digest as evidence, so export SOURCE_REVISION from git before the build.

steps: 0. Pre-checks, read-only. Record the current image: docker inspect audit-core-service --format '{{.Image}} {{ index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.revision" }}'. Open psql: docker exec -it controlplane-postgres sh -c 'psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"'. Run: SELECT version, applied_at FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY version; and SELECT count(*) FROM audit_events; If 007 is missing, the first boot of the new image applies 007 to 010, and that cannot be undone safely.

1. Env setup (lead decides, see open questions). Make the 11 service env files the runner requires present in the worktree's apps/Control Plane (all gitignored by .env*), and point the runner at the stack's live ledger rather than the worktree's own. Example: export CONTROL_PLANE_SECRETS_FILE="C:/dev/CoresSystem/apps/Control Plane/.env.generated-secrets". Then decide how the switch gets in: either apply D1-296 (add AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED: "${AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED:-0}" to the audit-core environment block) or set AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED=1 in the audit-core/.env this build reads.

2. Rebuild and switch on, from the worktree's apps/Control Plane: SOURCE_REVISION=$(git rev-parse HEAD) AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED=1 AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY_INTERVAL=5m bash scripts/run-control-plane.sh up -d --build --no-deps audit-core. --no-deps keeps postgres, NATS and the provisioner as they are; the provisioner code does not differ between main and model-plane. AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY_INTERVAL is optional and only shortens the verifier loop.

3. Confirm the boot. docker logs audit-core-service should show 'schema migrated', 'audit chain catch-up complete' (chained=0) and 'audit-core durable subscribers ready'. The warning 'audit chain is on without a signing key' must NOT appear if attestations are wanted. Check the switch with docker exec audit-core-service printenv AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED (expect 1). Check the key without printing it: docker exec audit-core-service sh -c '[ -n "$AUDIT_CHAIN_PRIVATE_KEY_BASE64" ] && echo key-set || echo key-unset'. Check readiness: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8187/readyz (primary, model and application buses ready). In psql: SELECT version FROM schema_migrations WHERE version >= '007' ORDER BY 1; (expect 007 to 010) and SELECT * FROM audit_chain_heads; (expect empty, or only orgs from earlier runs).

4. Cause one tool action. Sign in to Verevon and send a chat turn that makes the model call knowledge_search or web_search, for example 'search my documents for <topic>'. Expect two rows for your org: events tool_action_reserved and tool_action, plane 'model', source_producer 'session-core'. Check with: SELECT id, org_id, chain_seq, event, plane, chain_mode, ingested_at FROM audit_events WHERE chain_seq IS NOT NULL ORDER BY org_id, chain_seq;

5. Contiguity, linkage and genesis query: WITH c AS (SELECT org_id, chain_seq, prev_hash, row_hash, lag(chain_seq) OVER w AS p_seq, lag(row_hash) OVER w AS p_hash FROM audit_events WHERE chain_seq IS NOT NULL WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY org_id ORDER BY chain_seq)) SELECT org_id, count(*) AS rows, min(chain_seq), max(chain_seq), count(*) FILTER (WHERE p_seq IS NOT NULL AND chain_seq <> p_seq + 1) AS gaps, count(*) FILTER (WHERE p_seq IS NOT NULL AND prev_hash IS DISTINCT FROM p_hash) AS link_breaks, bool_and(p_seq IS NOT NULL OR (chain_seq = 1 AND prev_hash = sha256(convert_to('VAC1/genesis/' || org_id, 'UTF8')))) AS genesis_ok FROM c GROUP BY org_id; Expect gaps=0, link_breaks=0, genesis_ok=true and min=1, unless pruned.

6. Head equals last row, plus legacy and pending counts: SELECT h.org_id, h.head_seq, h.state, h.activated_at, t.chain_seq AS last_seq, h.head_hash = t.row_hash AS head_is_last_row, (SELECT count(*) FROM audit_events e WHERE e.org_id = h.org_id AND e.chain_seq IS NULL AND e.ingested_at < h.activated_at) AS legacy_unchained, (SELECT count(*) FROM audit_events e WHERE e.org_id = h.org_id AND e.chain_seq IS NULL AND e.ingested_at >= h.activated_at) AS pending_unchained FROM audit_chain_heads h LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT chain_seq, row_hash FROM audit_events e WHERE e.org_id = h.org_id AND e.chain_seq IS NOT NULL ORDER BY chain_seq DESC LIMIT 1) t ON true; Expect head_seq = last_seq, head_is_last_row = true, state = 'ok', pending_unchained = 0.

7. Capture the histogram before the restart: docker exec audit-core-service wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:9091/metrics | grep -E '^audit_core_chain_(head_lock_wait_seconds|appends_total|broken_total)'. Or through Prometheus: http://127.0.0.1:19095/api/v1/query?query=audit_core_chain_head_lock_wait_seconds_bucket and ...?query=histogram_quantile(0.99,sum by (le)(rate(audit_core_chain_head_lock_wait_seconds_bucket[15m]))). Prometheus must be running: bash scripts/run-control-plane.sh up -d controlplane-prometheus.

8. Restart mid-stream. Note SELECT max(chain_seq) FROM audit_events WHERE org_id = '<org>'; then run docker stop audit-core-service. While it is down, send 2 or 3 more tool-using chat turns; they queue in JetStream on model-nats. Then docker start audit-core-service. (Alternative: docker restart audit-core-service during a multi-tool turn.) Re-run steps 5 and 6. Expect max(chain_seq) to rise by 2 per tool call with gaps=0 and link_breaks=0, and every new row to have chain_mode='insert' (the switch stayed on). A non-zero audit_core_chain_appends_total{result="duplicate"} shows a redelivery that was absorbed. Capture the step 7 metrics again; they reset on restart.

9. Read the verifier and attestor results. The verifier runs a pass at every boot. SELECT org_id, last_status, last_reason, first_broken_seq, verified_through_seq, legacy_unchained_rows, last_run_at FROM audit_chain_verifications; Expect verified or verified_with_legacy. Expect partial/no_attestation if no key is held, or if the attestor had not yet signed at boot; in that case restart once more or wait for the 5m interval. Then: SELECT org_id, chain_seq, key_id, signed_at FROM audit_chain_attestations ORDER BY signed_at DESC LIMIT 5; (requires a key; the attestor runs every 60s).

10. Optional, only if the gateway compliance routes are live (D1-388, D1-391): as owner or admin, fetch /api/v1/audit/compliance/keys, /manifest (save `data` only as manifest.json) and every page of /events?limit=1000. Then run: docker cp the files into the container, or use a local build of cmd/audit-verify, and run audit-verify -manifest manifest.json -key-id <id> -public-key <pub> -json page-*.json (expect exit 0).
11. Save the evidence under docs/compliance/evidence/: switch values (not secrets), image digest, the query outputs, the metrics captures, the verifier row (runbook §9).

12. Switch off. Run the same command as step 2 without --build, with AUDIT_CHAIN_ENABLED unset or 0 (or set back to 0 in audit-core/.env): bash scripts/run-control-plane.sh up -d --no-deps audit-core. Check that the logs no longer show 'audit chain catch-up complete'. Then SELECT count(*) FROM audit_events WHERE chain_seq IS NOT NULL; should be unchanged, and audit_chain_heads stays. Do NOT run the revert SQL files, and do NOT rebuild audit-core from the main checkout (branch main, pre-S2) while migration 007 is applied.

findings.item: Correction and extra risk: building from the worktree can mint new credentials into a live ledger
findings.detail: The report is right that the worktree runner stops with 'missing service environment file'. On presence alone, the worktree has none of the service .env files, no apps/Control Plane/.env and no repo-root .env. It does have its own .env.generated-secrets. The report understates the danger of working around this. lookup_value only searches the env files the runner loaded. When a key is not found, persist_if_missing APPENDS a freshly generated random value to the secrets file. DB_PASSWORD falls back to random_value, and many tokens and NATS passwords are handled the same way. The secrets file is read LAST, so a value appended there wins for every later run. Two failure modes follow. (1) With the worktree's own ledger, the runner gives audit-core a random DB_PASSWORD or NATS password, and audit-core fails Postgres or NATS auth. (2) With CONTROL_PLANE_SECRETS_FILE pointed at the main checkout's ledger, while the main plane .env and root .env are not loaded, any key that lives only in those files gets a random value appended to the main ledger. That silently overrides the live value on the next main-checkout bring-up and can break the whole Control Plane. Do not point the worktree runner at the main ledger.

findings.item: Old image against the migrated schema: when it actually fails (D1-294 nuance)
findings.detail: main's Purge runs DELETE FROM audit_events by age without setting audit.maintenance. Because the trigger is BEFORE ... FOR EACH ROW, the delete fails only when at least one row is older than AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS (default 365). The error then returns before the usage_events delete, so usage retention stops as well. Chained rows are safe from the old image: the guard refuses the delete. The old image's plain inserts still work against the nullable columns, but its rows stay unchained, and if the org already has a head they are chained by CatchUp the next time the chain is switched on. D1-294 is closed as intended behaviour (runbook §7.6). This matters because the main checkout (branch main, without 007) is the usual Control Plane deploy path, so a later routine `run-control-plane.sh up` from main silently puts the pre-S2 image back.

findings.item: Minor correction: a restart does not always trigger a full verify
findings.detail: The report says the boot pass recomputes every row, so a restart doubles as a full check. In fact each pass resumes from the stored cursor, and a pass is full only when a full run is in progress, no full run has happened yet (LastFullAt is zero), or the last full run is older than 7×interval. For a chain activated during this proof, the first pass per org is full, so the claim holds for D1-297, but not in general. The boot pass also runs once, at start. To see a verifier row written after the tool action without restarting, set AUDIT_CHAIN_VERIFY_INTERVAL short (for example 30s; anything >= 1s is accepted).

findings.item: Confirmed: org activation, catch-up and genesis
findings.detail: The head is created by INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING followed by SELECT ... FOR UPDATE. activated_at takes DEFAULT NOW(), and ingested_at also defaults to NOW() in the same transaction, so the first chained row is not legacy. CatchUp only lists orgs that already have a head. findings.item: (1) The URL and the response field names a page fetch must use
findings.detail:
Use the relative path GET /api/v1/chat/threads/{thread_id}/messages?limit=100[&before=<message_id>]. It is mounted at chat.rs:58-61 and handled by json_handlers::get_thread_messages. The BFF checks the query first and then hands model-gateway's JSON back as-is, with no {data} envelope (shared.rs:700-703). So the page reads the snake_case body model-gateway builds: top-level `thread_id`, `messages[]` and `has_more`. Each message has `message_id` (left out when empty), `role`, `content`, `agent_name` and `author_subject_id` (each left out when empty), plus any metadata keys flattened onto the message. A paged read always carries `has_more`, and its value can be false. An unpaged read has no `has_more` key. Inside a page, messages are in conversation order, oldest first, so the next cursor is `messages[0].message_id`. The /messages route never uses camelCase `hasMore`. That spelling belongs to the different route /api/v1/chat/threads/{id}/transcript, which returns {data:{transcript:{turns[{id,...}]}, hasMore}}; the proof does not use it.

What each refused query hits:
- limit=0, limit=201 and limit=fifty: the BFF refuses them, 400 with {error:{code:"invalid_request", message:"limit must be a whole number from 1 to 200."}}.
- before without a limit: the BFF refuses it with "before needs a limit."
- before=a%26limit%3D1: axum decodes it to `a&limit=1`, which is not a valid id, so the BFF answers "before must be a message id."
- The foreign cursor (a real id from a different thread) passes the BFF's shape check. Session-core then refuses it with InvalidArgument. Model-gateway turns that into 400 {error:{code:"invalid_thread_request", message:"before_message_id does not name a message in this thread"}}, and the BFF passes the 400 through unchanged.

Other behaviour on the read path:
- Model-gateway caps the limit silently at the ceiling and does not refuse it.
- Session-core clamps the limit to 1..200, fetches limit+1 rows newest first, sets has_more = rows > limit, then puts the page back in conversation order.
- The cursor's sequence is looked up inside the thread's own org join.

findings.item: (2) How a page fetch learns the signed-in user's org id and user id
findings.detail:
GET /api/v1/session/current returns the envelope {data:{user:{id,email,name,emailVerified,image,role}, org:{id,name,role}|null, permissions, onboardingStatus, status}}. The values to seed are `data.user.id` and `data.org.id`. org.id is the session's active_org_id, or else the primary org from user-core. GET /api/v1/me/session-context returns the same org as `orgs[0].id`.

What the read actually authorizes against is different. It uses the org and subject inside the session-core and model-gateway tokens, which auth-core mints from the same cookie and binds to the active organization. Model-gateway passes claims.org_id on as ListConversationRequest.org_id. Session-core then checks that the thread row's org_id equals the caller's org and that the row's user_id equals the caller's user.

In the normal single-org case the session/current values match. This is not proven for a user who has switched org recently or who has more than one org. Uncertain: model-gateway falls back to a dev bearer when minting fails, and that bearer's org may differ. The seed can be checked before the proof:
- 200 on /messages: the seed matches the signed-in user.
- 404 thread_not_found: the thread row was not found.
- 403 forbidden: the org or user does not match ("tenant access denied" or the user check).

The seeded thread also appears in GET /api/v1/chat/threads, because its origin defaults to 'chat'.

findings.item: (2) The rows the seed needs in session-core's database, and why they are readable by their owner
findings.detail:
threads columns:
- NOT NULL with no default: `id`, `session_key`, `org_id`, `user_id` (0001). These are exactly what the script's INSERT supplies. user_id must be 1-128 characters (0017).
- NOT NULL with a default: `created_at`, `origin` ('chat', 0034), `source_scope` ('workspace', 0038), `persona_enabled` (true, 0042), `last_activity_at` (now(), 0049), `memory_mode` ('inherit', 0067).
- Everything else is nullable: presentation and pin/archive (0021), space context (0023), recipient_audience_revision and recipient_audience_hash (0024), the autonomy grant (0050), memory_resumed_at (0068).
- The CHECKs are satisfied by leaving space_id NULL with origin 'chat': threads_space_context_complete_chk, threads_recipient_audience_revision_complete_chk and threads_origin_space_consistency_chk. These CHECKs are NOT VALID, but that only skips rows that already existed; new inserts are still checked.

messages columns:
- NOT NULL with no default: `id`, `thread_id` (FK to threads), `role`, `content` (0001). `sequence` is GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY and must not be supplied. `metadata` defaults to '{}', which the read turns into no metadata.
- The nullable columns the read selects or filters on are agent_name (0030), author_subject_id (0035) and recipient_audience_revision (0025). client_message_id (0052) is nullable.

No other row is needed. The owner path is used when the request carries no Space decision. It only reads threads.org_id, threads.user_id and COALESCE(space_id,''), and it needs no Space, audience revision or retention row. The audience ceiling is NULL on that path, so the ceiling filter on messages never excludes a row. Nothing references messages by FK. FKs to threads come from messages, from runs and other tables in 0001, from plan_steps and todos (0003) and from scheduled_step_receipts (0029). The read path writes none of those rows.

The read SQL needs migrations 0025, 0030 and 0035 applied on the stack's database. Without them the read fails as an internal error, which model-gateway maps to 502. Migration 0055 adds a GIN full-text index on content, which the seeded rows also enter; this is harmless.

findings.item: (4) The SQL to seed the rows and, after the proof, delete exactly those rows
findings.detail:
Run it with psql against session-core's database, passing these variables (none is a credential):
- -v prefix=ws09s8-<YYYYMMDDtHHMMSSz>
- -v org=<data.org.id>
- -v usr=<data.user.id>

SEED:
```sql
BEGIN;
INSERT INTO threads (id, session_key, org_id, user_id)
VALUES (:'prefix' || '-thread', :'prefix' || '-thread', :'org', :'usr'),
       (:'prefix' || '-other',  :'prefix' || '-other',  :'org', :'usr');
INSERT INTO messages (id, thread_id, role, content)
SELECT :'prefix' || '-m' || lpad(n::text, 4, '0'), :'prefix' || '-thread',
       CASE WHEN n % 2 = 0 THEN 'user' ELSE 'assistant' END, 'turn ' || n
  FROM generate_series(0, 399) AS n ORDER BY n;
INSERT INTO messages (id, thread_id, role, content)
VALUES (:'prefix' || '-foreign', :'prefix' || '-other', 'user', 'turn elsewhere');
COMMIT;
SELECT thread_id, count(*), min(sequence), max(sequence) FROM messages
 WHERE thread_id IN (:'prefix' || '-thread', :'prefix' || '-other') GROUP BY thread_id;
```
Expect 400 messages in -thread and 1 in -other.

PLAN CHECK (the script's last step, lines 115-116):
```sql
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) SELECT m.id::text, m.role, m.content, m.agent_name, m.metadata, m.author_subject_id FROM messages m JOIN threads t ON t.id = m.thread_id WHERE m.thread_id = :'prefix' || '-thread' AND t.org_id = :'org' AND m.sequence < (SELECT max(sequence) FROM messages WHERE thread_id = :'prefix' || '-thread') ORDER BY m.sequence DESC LIMIT 101;
```
Expect a backward index scan on idx_messages_thread_id.

CLEANUP (exact ids, no LIKE, because `_` is a LIKE wildcard):
```sql
BEGIN;
SELECT count(*) FROM messages WHERE thread_id IN (:'prefix' || '-thread', :'prefix' || '-other');  -- expect 401
DELETE FROM messages WHERE thread_id IN (:'prefix' || '-thread', :'prefix' || '-other');           -- expect DELETE 401
DELETE FROM threads WHERE id IN (:'prefix' || '-thread', :'prefix' || '-other');                    -- expect DELETE 2
COMMIT;
```
If a count differs, ROLLBACK. If the threads DELETE hits a FK error, something wrote a run, todo, plan_step or receipt for these threads; most likely someone opened the thread in the SPA. In that case ROLLBACK and investigate instead of cascading.

About the order of turns: Postgres assigns the identity values in the rows' output order, so the ORDER BY normally gives sequence values in n order. This is not formally guaranteed, but the order check in the proof would catch a violation.

findings.item: (5) How the BFF image is deployed, and what C:/dev/tools/swap_gateway_image.py keeps
findings.detail:
The script does not build anything. It swaps the running container verevon-gateway-rs onto an image that must already be tagged `frontend-plane-verevonv3-gateway:latest`. It does this without `docker compose`, because a plain compose call fails on missing secrets.

The swap:
1. Runs docker inspect on the live container.
2. Stops it and renames it to verevon-gateway-rs-pre-fix-rollback.
3. Runs a new container with these settings copied over:
   - restart policy, --init, user and working dir
   - the first network and its aliases (any further networks are connected after the start, with their aliases)
   - host port bindings, including the host IP
   - every Env entry except PATH, HOSTNAME and HOME
   - bind mounts (with :ro when read-only) and volumes, named or anonymous
   - the CMD or CMD-SHELL healthcheck with its interval, timeout, start period and retries
   - the entrypoint and cmd
4. Waits up to about 60 s for health.
5. On failure, removes the new container and restores the old one by renaming it back and starting it.

What it does not carry over: compose labels (so compose stops tracking the container), extra_hosts, cap_add/cap_drop, security_opt, read_only, tmpfs mounts, resource limits, logging config, static IP, DNS, stop signal and timeout, ulimits and health start-interval.

Caveats:
- The Env it copies includes the old image's baked-in ENV values, and the old Entrypoint and Cmd override the new image's own.
- A new env var would have to be added by hand; paging needs none.
- On success it leaves the stopped -pre-fix-rollback container behind. It stops the live gateway and renames it before its try block (lines 94-95). So a second run while that rollback container still exists stops the gateway, then fails at the rename, and exits with the gateway left stopped and no automatic recovery. Remove or rename the old rollback container (after checking it is no longer needed) before re-running the script.

findings.item: Missed: session-core's background Dreaming worker will mine the 401 seeded turns as the real user's conversation
findings.detail:
session-core always starts `dreaming::run`, which by default runs every 300 s in batches of 100. Its `load_pending_messages` selects every message with role 'user' or 'assistant' that has no `dream_runs` row yet. It joins threads only for org_id, user_id, source_scope and memory_resumed_at. It does not filter on `threads.memory_mode`, origin or thread age. So within about 20 minutes all 401 seeded turns will be read for the signed-in user:
- One `dream_runs` row is written per message, with thread_id set and metadata.message_id holding the seeded id. There is no FK, so nothing blocks the delete, but the rows are left behind.
- The turns go to the extractor. If an LLM extractor is configured, that means model calls on "turn N" text. Letta writes are also possible.
- `agent_memory` rows could be saved for the real user, although "turn N" is unlikely to yield a memory.

The report's cleanup does not mention `dream_runs`, and the visible part of the report never mentions this worker.

To limit it: seed the threads with memory_mode 'off'. A dreaming test shows a save into a thread set off is refused at the write, but the messages are still read. Then delete the seeded `dream_runs` rows and check `agent_memory` during cleanup. Running the proof quickly is not a fix: the interval's first tick fires at once, and later ticks can land inside the window.

findings.item: Missed: the seeded thread appears at the top of the real user's chat list, and using it there blocks the cleanup
findings.detail:
origin defaults to 'chat' and last_activity_at to now(), so the seeded probe thread and the second 'other' thread both appear in the signed-in user's chat sidebar. Opening one is a read and is harmless. Sending a message in one, or starting a run there, writes `runs` and other rows that have NOT NULL FKs to threads(id). After that, the cleanup's `DELETE FROM threads` fails with an FK violation. Thread erasure deletes in a fixed order because most of these FKs have no ON DELETE CASCADE.

To avoid it, either seed origin 'system', which passes both origin CHECKs with space_id NULL and which the list_conversation read path never checks, or tell the operator not to touch the two threads in the UI. In either case the cleanup should first count rows in runs, memory_index, plan_steps, todos and scheduled_step_receipts for the two ids.

findings.item: Item (5), BFF environment: the BFF needs no new variable, but model-gateway's ceiling variable can break the proof

The BFF's page limit is a compile-time constant (MAX_THREAD_MESSAGES_PAGE = 200). No environment variable enables paging in the BFF, and no feature switch exists (the SPA flag belongs to WS09-S9).

findings.detail:
What the script carries over to the new container, read from `docker inspect` of the running one:
- Every Env entry except PATH, HOSTNAME and HOME. This includes ENV values baked into the old image.
- The restart policy, init, user and working directory.
- The first network and its aliases; the other networks are reconnected with their aliases.
- The port bindings, bind mounts (with their ro flag) and named or anonymous volumes.
- The healthcheck command, interval, timeout, start period and retries.
- The entrypoint and cmd.

The image is always `frontend-plane-verevonv3-gateway:latest`.

What it does NOT carry over, compared with the compose definition:
- security_opt no-new-privileges and cap_drop ALL
- the 256M memory and 0.75 CPU limits
- the json-file log rotation (10m x 3)
- stop_grace_period 20s
- the compose labels, so compose no longer recognises the container

1. Line 94, `docker stop verevon-gateway-rs`, succeeds.
2. Line 95, `docker rename`, fails on the name conflict.
3. Those two lines are outside the try block, so no rollback runs. The script exits and leaves the live gateway stopped.

findings.item: Item (4), seed SQL: psql variables need stdin or -f, and the order of `sequence`
findings.detail:
`:'prefix'` and the other variables are expanded by psql only when the SQL comes from stdin or `-f`. With `psql -c`, `:'prefix'` reaches the server unexpanded and the statement fails. Use a heredoc or a file. Per the Bash heredoc limit note, write the file first and pass it with -f.

The INSERT ... SELECT ... ORDER BY n relies on identity values being assigned in sort order. Postgres does this for a single-sort plan, and the proof script relies on it too. The seed's own check, min/max(sequence) and count per thread, is enough to confirm it.

steps: Before the swap, run `docker ps -a --filter name=verevon-gateway-rs-pre-fix-rollback`. If the container exists, remove it. Otherwise swap_gateway_image.py stops the live gateway and then fails on the rename, outside its rollback.

Build the BFF from this worktree, not the main checkout: `docker build -t frontend-plane-verevonv3-gateway:latest "apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway"`. Then run C:/dev/tools/swap_gateway_image.py. Afterwards, re-apply or accept the loss of cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, the memory/CPU limits and log rotation, which the swap drops.

Rebuild session-core and model-gateway from the worktree, both of them, together with the BFF. Use the plane's compose.sh. Per the memory note 'Worktree Model Plane deploy drops live env', then run recreate-with-live-env.sh. Confirm by name only that MODEL_GATEWAY_THREAD_MESSAGES_MAX_LIMIT is unset or at least 100 on the live model-gateway.
From the signed-in page, GET /api/v1/session/current must answer 200, which proves the SPA still reaches the swapped gateway under the `gateway` alias. Read data.user.id and data.org.id.
Run a read-only cross-check of the org in session-core's database: `SELECT DISTINCT org_id FROM threads WHERE user_id = :'usr' AND origin = 'chat';`. Use that org if it differs from session/current.

Seed through `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v prefix=... -v org=... -v usr=... -f seed.sql`, not -c. Seed both threads with `memory_mode` 'off', and with origin 'system' to keep them out of the user's chat list. Example: `INSERT INTO threads (id, session_key, org_id, user_id, origin, memory_mode) VALUES (:'prefix'||'-thread', :'prefix'||'-thread', :'org', :'usr', 'system', 'off'), (:'prefix'||'-other', :'prefix'||'-other', :'org', :'usr', 'system', 'off');`. The messages INSERTs stay the same as the script's.
Do not open or post in the seeded threads from the UI during the proof.
Run the JavaScript summary from the page. Then run the script's EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) query (script line 116) in psql with the same prefix and org.

Before cleanup, count the FK-dependent rows. Each count must be 0, or the threads delete will fail: `SELECT 'runs', count(*) FROM runs WHERE thread_id IN (:'prefix'||'-thread', :'prefix'||'-other') UNION ALL SELECT 'memory_index', count(*) FROM memory_index WHERE thread_id IN (...) UNION ALL SELECT 'plan_steps', count(*) FROM plan_steps WHERE thread_id IN (...) UNION ALL SELECT 'todos', count(*) FROM todos WHERE thread_id IN (...) UNION ALL SELECT 'scheduled_step_receipts', count(*) FROM scheduled_step_receipts WHERE thread_id IN (...);`. Also check for memories created from the seeded turns: `SELECT count(*) FROM agent_memory WHERE source_links::text LIKE '%' || :'prefix' || '%';`. That column's shape is unverified, so delete nothing from agent_memory without reviewing the rows.

Cleanup, in one transaction: `BEGIN; DELETE FROM dream_runs WHERE thread_id IN (:'prefix'||'-thread', :'prefix'||'-other'); DELETE FROM messages WHERE thread_id IN (:'prefix'||'-thread', :'prefix'||'-other'); DELETE FROM threads WHERE id IN (:'prefix'||'-thread', :'prefix'||'-other'); COMMIT;`. Expect 0 to 401 dream_runs rows, 401 messages and 2 threads. Then re-count all three to confirm 0.
